notes: Route evidence is contested across practitioner sources; see verification issue V-002.

aliases.notes: Not a synonym. Analytical characterisation of the TB-500 formulation identifies it as Ac-LKKTETQ, the N-terminally acetylated 17-23 fragment of this peptide: seven residues of forty-three, about one fifth of the mass. Practitioner sources and some 2026 peer-reviewed papers use the two names interchangeably; this index does not, and keeps a separate record for the fragment. Verification issue V-001, resolved 13 September 2026 by SRC-041 and SRC-042 and left open on the separate question of what any given product contains (SRC-043).

notes: Has genuine human trial evidence, which is unusual in this register and is attached to the full-length peptide rather than to the name practitioners use.

aliases.notes: Formulations with and without a drug affinity complex differ materially in duration. Sources are not always explicit about which is meant.

notes: Investigational. Development status is time-sensitive and must be re-checked before any publication. Verification issue V-003.

aliases.notes: The sequence the analytical literature identifies in the TB-500 formulation.
Sold alongside TB-500 and analysed with it in SRC-043, which found product contents inconsistent with their descriptions. No source held here establishes what TB1000 is.

Widely used for this substance and incorrect: thymosin beta-4 is the full 43-residue peptide, of which this is residues 17-23. Recorded as a misnomer rather than a synonym so that search surfaces the confusion instead of resolving it.

notes: Kept as a record of its own because the evidence says it is a different molecule from Thymosin beta-4. Evidence must not cross between the two.
